items.raw_excerpt:

Instead of generating a modal from patterns, why not fetch the actual UntitledUI modal? How it works:
- AI says "add a settings modal"
- MCP fetches the real component + all base dependencies (buttons, inputs, etc.)
- Files are placed in your project with correct imports Tools available:
- search_components: Find by name/description
- get_component_with_deps: Fetch with all dependencies
- get_example: Fetch complete page templates (dashboards, landing pages) Requires UntitledUI Pro license for premium components. Base components are free. GitHub: https://git

items.title: Sentinel – Zero-trust governance for AI Agents
items.raw_excerpt: Hi HN, I’m a software engineer and I’ve been building agentic workflows lately. Like many of you, I got concerned about giving LLMs "write access" to tools. Whether it's a payment API, a database deletion, or a simple email send, the risk of a hallucination causing a $5k mistake is real. I wanted a way to keep a human in the loop without rewriting my entire agent logic every time. So I built Sentinel. It’s a lightweight Python layer that wraps any tool/function. The key principles I focused on: Fail-secure by default: If the rules engine or the network fails, the action is blocked. Most systems fail-open, which is a nightmare for security. items.raw_excerpt: 为防止大语言模型和 AI Agent 执行嵌入在外部数据中的恶意指令， 所有进入 Agent 上下文的文本在完成校验之前都必须被视为不可信数据 ，其中不仅包括用户输入的提示，还包括来自外部系统的各类信息。AI 安全公司 CyberArk 的首席软件架构师 Niv Rabin 表示。为此，他所在的团队提出了一种基于“指令检测”（Instruction Detection）与“历史感知校验”（History-Aware Validation）的方法，用于同时防御恶意输入数据和上下文历史投毒攻击。

title_i18n.zh: AI Agent 是长期运行的“风险系统”，如果你还只在防 Prompt Injection，说明已经落后一代了
title_i18n.en: AI Agents are long-running "risk systems." If you're still only guarding against Prompt Injection, you're already a generation behind.
title_i18n.es: AI Agent es un "sistema de riesgo" de larga duración; si aún solo te proteges del Prompt Injection, significa que ya estás una generación atrasado.

excerpt_i18n.zh: 为防止大语言模型和 AI Agent 执行嵌入在外部数据中的恶意指令， 所有进入 Agent 上下文的文本在完成校验之前都必须被视为不可信数据 ，其中不仅包括用户输入的提示，还包括来自外部系统的各类信息。AI 安全公司 CyberArk 的首席软件架构师 Niv Rabin 表示。为此，他所在的团队提出了一种基于“指令检测”（Instruction Detection）与“历史感知校验”（History-Aware Validation）的方法，用于同时防御恶意输入数据和上下文历史投毒攻击。
excerpt_i18n.en: To prevent large language models and AI Agents from executing malicious instructions embedded in external data, all text entering the Agent context must be treated as untrusted data until verification is completed. This includes not only user-input prompts but also various types of information from external systems, according to Niv Rabin, Chief Software Architect at AI security company CyberArk. To address this, his team has proposed a method based on "Instruction Detection" and "History-Aware Validation" to defend against both malicious input data and context history poisoning attacks simultaneously.
excerpt_i18n.es: Para evitar que los modelos de lenguaje extenso y los agentes de IA ejecuten instrucciones maliciosas incrustadas en datos externos, todo texto que ingrese al contexto del agente debe considerarse como datos no confiables hasta que se complete la verificación. Esto incluye no solo las indicaciones ingresadas por el usuario, sino también diversos tipos de información proveniente de sistemas externos, señaló Niv Rabin, arquitecto jefe de software de la empresa de seguridad cibernética CyberArk. Para abordar esto, su equipo propuso un enfoque basado en "detección de instrucciones" y "validación consciente del historial".

Author | Zhao Zhiqi  Editor | Bao Yonggang  
Before the first snow of January fell in Beijing, we met Professor Zhai Jidong at Tsinghua University. Holding a thermal cup, he spoke briskly, with almost no pauses or ambiguities even while thinking and narrating simultaneously.  
This tenured professor from Tsinghua’s Department of Computer Science, who has led his team to win 15 world supercomputing championships, is now dissecting an industry anomaly:  
Why, amid the soaring parameters of large models and the declining cost of computing power, are users’ burdens for AI implementation becoming increasingly heavy?  
He points out that high scores on benchmarks may not always align with users’ actual needs. Sometimes, the same model can perform vastly differently across various MaaS platforms, as some providers apply “castration-level” quantization to reduce costs. Faced with a dizzying array of MaaS suppliers, users must weigh performance, price, and stability, often exhausting their energy just by surveying market quotes.  
“Leaving the initiative of model selection entirely to users is actually a significant challenge,” Zhai Jidong states frankly. This “paradox of choice” not only torments developers but also erodes corporate profits. For enterprises, the core of cost reduction and efficiency improvement may not lie in pursuing the most cutting-edge models, but in how to deploy appropriately capable models—using expensive large models for complex instructions and lightweight small models for routine tasks.  
Recognizing this pain point, Qingcheng Jizhi, an AI infrastructure startup founded by several of Zhai Jidong’s former students, has developed an intelligent routing system.
